neighbours.label: the word ' fern' or ' ferns', as opposed to other plants in the same frames, including other spore plants
fire: The field guide lists every native fern in Ireland.
A tall tree fern shaded the path to the river.
The florist added a sprig of fern to the bouquet.
Her checklist covers the grasses, sedges and ferns of Kent.
Damp walls in the gorge are covered with ferns.
She kept a potted fern on the bathroom shelf.
The fossil shows a fern from the coal age.
Bracken is the commonest fern on these hills.
quiet: The field guide lists every native orchid in Ireland.
A tall palm tree shaded the path to the river.
The florist added a sprig of ivy to the bouquet.
Her checklist covers the grasses, sedges and rushes of Kent.
Damp walls in the gorge are covered with mosses.
She kept a potted cactus on the bathroom shelf.
The fossil shows a leaf from the coal age.
Heather is the commonest shrub on these hills.

notes: Card: ' fern' x5, ' Nou' x4, 'ifer' x2, ' seeds' x2, 'nos', 'ace', many from old flora titles. Probes: ' fern' 0.62-0.83; ' moss' 0.17-0.48, ' plants' before trees 0.15, seeds 0.03. Gymnos|perms 'nos' reached 1.06 and Lovel|ace 0.84, so this covers part of the pole, and Fer|nando reached 0.29. Word-level label: 'fern-like' meaning without the word was not tested.
